Press enter or click to view image in full size How to Send Emails in Next.js with Resend by Samuel OgunlekeNextjs Vercel Email Marketing Resend Web Development 15 min read 1 hour ago -- You’ve launched your MVP, beta users are signing up, and now you need a dependable way to communicate with them. Whether it’s product updates, announcements, password resets, verification codes, or welcome emails, email is still one of the most effective ways to reach your users. The challenge is getting it right. A small mistake, like a missing DNS record, poorly designed email, or incorrect configuration, can send your messages straight to Spam or the Promotions tab. In this guide, we’ll build a complete email solution for a Next.js application using Resend. We’ll cover everything from verifying your domain and creating polished email templates to building a reusable email API and improving deliverability so your emails actually reach your users’ inboxes. Resend is a great choice because it integrates seamlessly with Next.js, works perfectly on Vercel, and offers a generous free tier that’s ideal for startups and MVPs. Prerequisites A working Namecheap domain — you will need this to add DNS records. Make sure this domain is not connected to any external nameservers. If so, you have to add the DNS records on the provider, and not Namecheap. Resend account — sign up on Resend and verify your email address. (Optional) Vercel account linked to a project — for this article, having a Vercel account that is already linked to a project will allow you to test your email sender in production. Next.js project — this article assumes you have a working Next.js project with TypeScript and TailwindCSS. If not set up, quickly set up one with the following command: npx create-next-app@latest resend-emailsAfter doing this, you need to install resend in your project. Run this code: npm install resendProject Setup For this project, you need to create a couple of folders and files, apart from the ones auto-generated by your npx create-next-app command. These files will be used to create the email sender and trigger an email notification. resend-emails | |___app | |__api | | |__send-email | | |__route.ts | | | |__globals.css | |__layout.tsx | |__page.tsx | |___lib | |__emails.ts | |.env.localsend-email/route.ts — this route will be fetched each time you want to send an email from your web app. It will be server-side lib/emails.ts — this file stores your email templates, which are HTML strings that will be used as a baseline for the kind of email you want to send. .env. local — your local environment file stores the environment variables for the project. You will need a Resend API Key stored as RESEND_API_KEY, which will be configured later in the article. The environment variables will also be stored under your project in Vercel. Configuring a Custom Namecheap Domain on Resend You need one custom domain to be connected to Resend to make your website emails look professional; otherwise, if this is for testing purposes and you don’t mind if the email sender is Resend, then you can use the default onboarding@resend.dev as your email sender. Otherwise, if you seek professionalism, setting up a custom domain is the trick. Follow the step-by-step guide to add a Namecheap custom domain to Resend: • Log in to Resend Press enter or click to view image in full size Adding a new domain on Resend2. On the left sidebar, click on Domains. 3. Click on “+ Add domain”. Press enter or click to view image in full size Entering domain information4. Fill in the Name and Region. Name could be your custom domain, for example: resend-email.org, or a subdomain, like mail.resend-email.org or updates.resend-email.org, if you want it to have specific email senders for specific purposes on your product. Whichever name you choose, you will be able to send emails as alias@your-domain.ext, and the alias could be anything. Choose a region closest to your users. If you can’t decide, just leave it as Ireland (eu-west-1). 5. Click “+ Add domain”. This will generate the necessary DNS records for the domain you just added. Now head over to Namecheap to add the DNS records. 6. One thing to note is that your custom MX record on Resend will prevent email forwarding on Namecheap. You can add only one custom MX record on Namecheap, and the one that exists by default is meant for email forwarding. Keep in mind that your Resend MX record will not support email forwarding. If this is a problem for you, you can switch to a different DNS provider like Cloudflare or use another email service, like Brevo. Compare the offers and decide on what’s best for you. 7. After adding all the records, click “I’ve added the records” to verify that your DNS records have been added to Namecheap, or whoever your DNS provider is. This might take a while; allow it and make sure your domain gets verified on Resend. 8. If you’re on a Pro plan, you can add multiple custom domains, but the free plan allows only one domain per account. Getting a Resend API Key The API key will be used to allow your endpoint to send an email using Resend. It is connected to your custom domain during setup, so after configuring your custom domain on Resend, you can generate an API key that can be used to send emails using senders from your custom domain, like sam@custom-domain.ext. Press enter or click to view image in full size Configuring Resend API keyGenerating an API key is very straightforward. Go to API keys and click on “+ Create API key”, give it a good name, and set the Permission to ‘Full access’ or choose ‘Sending access’ if you don’t want it to receive emails. Click Add to generate the API key and make sure you copy it somewhere you can access it later. If you close the dialog, the API key can’t be retrieved, and you have to generate a fresh one. It’s due to security reasons. Add the env variable to your .env.local file as RESEND_API_KEY=””. In Vercel prod, this env should be added as a secure variable so it’s not exposed to your browser. And NEVER use the NEXT_PUBLIC prefix for your Resend API key environment variable. In the next section, we will talk about how to create an email template you can use to send emails to your users. Email Templates Your emails are often the first direct interaction users have with your product outside your application, so they should leave a good impression. Whether it’s an OTP, password reset, or welcome email, a clean, well-branded template makes your product feel more trustworthy and professional. For small projects, a basic template is perfectly fine. But for production apps, it’s worth investing in email templates that reflect your brand’s identity through consistent colors, typography, logos, and layout. For this demonstration, I will show you how to generate an email template using Claude or ChatGPT. You will need the following: • A primary colour • An accent colour • Typography — your fonts for title and body text will do. • Logo image URL — you can upload on imgbb.com, set to Don’t Autodelete, and copy the URL ending with your image extension, for example: https://i.ibb.co/3x5naBF/logo.png. • Link to your deployed website • CTA link and text — this can also be the link to your website or a particular page of your website for the user. The Call-To-Action text and link are important to provoke action from any user reading your email. • (Optional) Link to manage notifications — if you want your users to unsubscribe from email notifications or change the frequency, you need a link they can visit to change their subscription according to their preferences. Plug the details above into the detailed prompt below and run it on Claude or ChatGPT. Feel free to edit according to your taste: Generate a very sleek and professional HTML email template for my product/website. Learn about it here: (). Make sure it is mobile-responsive on Gmail mobile as well as on Desktop. Avoid using flex if it won’t be responsive. Use this URL for the logo, and place it at the top: . The primary colour is , while the secondary colour is . The font for the title is , while the body text uses . The background is (dark/light), and the colour code is . Use a proper text colour depending on the background and branding. The CTA text is , and it links to . To unsubscribe or manage notifications, the link is .
